lessons.title: Talking About the Past

items.exampleMeaning: Yesterday I went to the cinema.

items.example: La semana pasada vi una película.
items.exampleMeaning: Last week I saw a movie.
I liked the book a lot.

lessons.tip: In Spanish, the past tense can be expressed with the preterite form. Remember to use 'fui' for 'I went' and 'fue' for 'it was' when talking about the past.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: What did you do yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: Yesterday I went to the cinema.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Did you like the movie?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I liked it a lot.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: La semana pasada, ¿fue divertida la fiesta?
dialogue.meaning: Last week, was the party fun?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: Yes, it was very fun.

scenario.partnerRole: A friend who wants to know about your past experiences.
scenario.brief: Ask your partner about their activities yesterday and last week. Share your own experiences using the past tense.
scenario.goal: You will share what you did and how you felt about it.

lessons.title: Expressing Likes and Dislikes

items.example: Me gustó más el libro que la película.
items.exampleMeaning: I liked the book more than the movie.
I enjoyed the dinner a lot.

lessons.tip: Use 'me encanta' to express strong liking and 'no me gusta' for dislikes. Remember to use the past tense forms when talking about past experiences.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Do you like music?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I love music.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: What did you think of the dinner?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: It seemed very good to me.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Te gustó más el libro o la película?
dialogue.meaning: Did you like the book or the movie more?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: I liked the book more.

scenario.partnerRole: A friend discussing preferences and experiences with you.
scenario.learnerRole: You, sharing your likes and dislikes.
scenario.brief: Ask your partner about their preferences. Share your opinions about past experiences using likes and dislikes.
scenario.goal: You will express what you love and dislike.

lessons.title: Sharing Experiences

items.exampleMeaning: I liked the food a lot.
I didn't go to the party.

lessons.tip: Use 'visité' for 'I visited' and 'tuve' for 'I had' when sharing experiences. These verbs help describe what you did in the past.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: ¿Visitaste a alguien el fin de semana?
dialogue.meaning: Did you visit anyone last weekend?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I visited my friends.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Did you go to an event?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I went to a concert.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Did you try a new restaurant?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, probé un nuevo restaurante y me gustó mucho.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I tried a new restaurant and I liked it a lot.

scenario.partnerRole: A friend excited to hear about your experiences.
scenario.brief: Ask your partner about their weekend activities. Share what you visited or tried recently.
scenario.goal: You will share your experiences and how you felt about them.

lessons.title: Reflecting on Experiences

items.exampleMeaning: It was exciting to see the concert.

items.example: No me esperaba que fuera tan bueno.
items.exampleMeaning: I didn't expect it to be so good.

items.example: Me quedé en casa para descansar.

lessons.tip: Use 'me sentí' to express feelings about experiences. This helps you describe how past events affected you.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: How did you feel at the concert?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: I felt happy and excited.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Was it exciting?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, fue emocionante ver a la banda.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, it was exciting to see the band.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Did anything surprise you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, me sorprendió lo bueno que fue.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I was surprised at how good it was.

scenario.partnerRole: A friend who wants to know how you felt about your experiences.
scenario.brief: Ask your partner how they felt about their recent experiences. Share your feelings about events and surprises.
scenario.goal: You will reflect on your feelings and share them.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: What did you do over the weekend?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Fui a la playa y me sentí feliz.
dialogue.meaning: I went to the beach and I felt happy.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Did you like the weather?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No me gustó, fue muy frío.
dialogue.meaning: I didn't like it, it was very cold.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Did you try a new restaurant?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Sí, probé un nuevo restaurante y me encantó.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I tried a new restaurant and I loved it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: How did you feel at the concert?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: I felt excited, it was incredible.

scenario.partnerRole: A friend who wants to review the chapter with you.
scenario.learnerRole: You, sharing your experiences and feelings.
scenario.brief: Discuss your weekend activities, likes, and feelings. Use the vocabulary and grammar from the chapter.
scenario.goal: You will practice speaking about your past experiences.
